hypothesis: If full-grown larvae of bees, wasps and caterpillars become a motionless hardened stage before the adult, public life-history accounts of a honey bee, a yellowjacket and a butterfly will describe a larva that becomes a pupa, chrysalis or cocoon, and public observations will record that pupal stage.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Animal Diversity Web accounts of Apis mellifera, Vespula maculifrons and Danaus plexippus must each contain a larval term (larva, larvae, caterpillar, grub) and a pupal term (pupa, pupae, chrysalis, cocoon) in a sentence that also has a transition (become, becomes, pupate, pupates, enter the pupal, molt, moult, transform, develops into, emerge). All three accounts must match. As a corroboration that does not replace the text rule, iNaturalist research-grade observations annotated Life Stage = Pupa must number at least 30 for each of the three taxa. The claim is supported only if all three accounts match and all three pupa counts are at least 30.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refutes if any account says there is no pupal stage, or describes hemimetabolous or incomplete metamorphosis without a pupa, for that taxon. Mixed if one or two accounts match the transition sentence and the others are silent, or if all three accounts match but any taxon has fewer than 30 pupa annotations while the account matched. Inconclusive with reason data-unavailable if none of the three accounts can be fetched. Inconclusive with reason not-operationalizable if the accounts can be fetched but none contains both a larval term and a pupal term and the iNaturalist life-stage vocabulary cannot be resolved.

test_contract.expected_observation: Each of the three accounts describes the larva becoming a pupa, chrysalis or cocoon, and each taxon has at least 30 research-grade pupa observations.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: An account of one of the three named insects denies a pupal stage or describes development from larva to adult without one.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public species accounts of one bee, one wasp and one butterfly or moth, plus a public observation store that annotates life stage. The three accounts stand for the three groups Aristotle names (bees, wasps, caterpillars). They are not a sample of all insects.
test_contract.inference_method: Sentence coding of the three accounts for a larva-to-pupa transition, and a count of iNaturalist observations whose controlled Life Stage value is Pupa. Support requires both. The observation count documents that the stage is recorded; the sentence documents the transition. Thresholds are all three accounts and 30 observations per taxon.

interpretation: Aristotle's motionless egg-like stage with a hardened husk is the pupa (chrysalis or cocoon). The test covers the three groups he names, one species each. It does not time immobility or measure cuticle hardness; those are taken as the ordinary definition of a pupa once the account uses that term for the post-larval stage. 'Pupa' in iNaturalist is that project's life-stage value, resolved at run time from the controlled-term list rather than from a hard-coded identifier.
caveats: The three ADW URLs and the iNaturalist controlled-term endpoint returned HTTP 200 on HEAD. No account body and no observation count was read.

A Dryad table of lepidopteran development times (10.5061/dryad.qjq2bvqk4) was considered and not used: file downloads returned an Anubis challenge page, so the development times were not opened and are not a planned dataset.
method: Downloaded the three Animal Diversity Web accounts and coded sentences that contain a larval term, a pupal term, and a transition verb. Resolved the iNaturalist Life Stage vocabulary and counted research-grade observations annotated Pupa for each taxon. Support required all three accounts and at least 30 pupa observations each.

measured.unit: accounts, of three, with a larva-to-pupa sentence
measured.uncertainty: one species account per named group; observation counts are annotations, not timed immobility
